newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves after recent rains.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves after recent rains.

text.p: The Texas wheat crop showed a general improvement during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.

"Fields were beginning to joint in the Plains and Cross Timbers (regions). Some dryland fields in the High Plains still needed additional moisture," the report said. "Fields were heading in some central areas and in south Texas."
Wheat was rated 18 percent excellent, 40 good, 36 fair, five poor and one very poor. That compared to last week's rating of 11 percent excellent, 49 good, 34 fair and six poor.
Two percent of Texas wheat acreage had headed, versus one percent last year and one percent for the five-year average.

Texas range and pasture conditions were rated six percent excellent, 27 good, 44 fair, 16 poor and seven very poor, compared to last week's rating of five percent excellent, 28 good, 43 fair, 17 poor and seven very poor.

Texas cotton acreage was two percent planted, compared to five percent last year and five percent on average. Corn acreage was 15 percent planted, versus 29 last year and 24 on average. Sorghum acreage was 11 percent planted, versus 23 last year and 20 percent on average.
